lines:
Corrected memo. Two statements in the previous memo were wrong and are fixed here: the loop bound is no longer required, and the claim that this codebase has no budget ledger was false.

Commits: 4bff26e (contract and region-aware validation), 2c4548d (executor, frames and evidence), 1595a7b (per-iteration identity), 1073870 (editor and route declarations), dac29c4 (nested coverage), 6321e0c (optional bound, no clock check).

Contract. A loop header declares a frozen exitCondition predicate and routes exactly one body, one exit and one fallback transition. maximumIterations is optional: a declared bound must be a positive whole number and is the author's own number, and an omitted (or explicitly empty) bound means the loop repeats until its exit condition holds. analyze_loop_regions is the single implementation used by both the validator and the compiler: the region is single-entry and single-exit, may not contain a wait or completion node, nests at most four deep, and only declared feedback edges may close a cycle. compile_graph_pass carries CompiledLoopV1 (routes, feedback edge, region in execution order, optional bound) and computes the order over the region-expanded graph.

Execution. The pass walks a work queue; the header owns its region, evaluates the frozen exit condition before each iteration and repeats the region under it. A declared bound that is reached takes the declared fallback route with an explicit limit-exceeded observation. Cancellation is observed between iterations, so Stop always ends a loop — which matters now that the exit condition can be the only natural stop. A suspension inside a region persists the active frames, so resume continues its own iteration and never replays settled work; stopped-pass continuations carry the same frames.

Limits and budgets, corrected. There is no aggregate run budget of any kind, and the worker ledger that does exist is inert for internal Agent runs: crates/aworkit-workflow-worker/src/limits.rs implements Budget/Usage/BudgetEnvelope/LimitLedger/LimitController, and pipeline.rs builds one for every run, but the desktop freezes every cumulative dimension to a sentinel — tokens and cost to MAX_SAFE_WIRE_INTEGER, and both budget.deadline_ms and deadline_epoch_millis to NO_AGGREGATE_RUN_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MILLIS, whose own comment states there is no aggregate run deadline and that usage is reported without a ceiling. The small figures (turns/attempts/actions = 1, depth/fanout/parallel) describe one outer brokered execution, and agent-internal provider calls are explicitly not turn-capped (legacy_maximum_turns: None). The frozen run_deadline_millis is inert legacy data with no consumer that builds a deadline from it. What remains are per-operation bounds (provider request timeout, transport retries, tool-output bytes, overflow retries, approval TTLs) and freeze-time structural validation, none of which cap a run's total work. The loop's deadline diversion added earlier was dormant because of that sentinel and has now been removed: a loop ends only on its exit condition, a declared bound, or the user stopping it.

Evidence. Every activity carries its loop frame (header, iteration, optional bound); exit-condition evaluations and limit outcomes are their own observations of the header; a repeated iteration is a distinct span, and the span details carry loopHeaderId, iteration and either maximumIterations or unbounded: true. An unbounded loop's opening observation says so in words.

Editor. The palette exposes the loop header with the predicate panel as its exit condition, an optional maximum-iterations field (empty means no cap; the numeric field now writes null when cleared rather than zero), and typed body/exit/fallback routes. A transition targeting a loop header that declares the feedback route closes that region, so neither the editor diagnostic nor Run admission reports a declared loop as a cycle; a missing feedback edge, a missing route, an undeclared back edge, a non-positive declared bound and a missing exit condition are each reported, while an undeclared bound is a named warning that never blocks a run.

Tests. Region metadata; undeclared cycle; missing feedback edge; missing routes; doubled feedback; second entry and exit; wait inside a region; predicate validation; a declared bound of 0, 1.5, -3 and 2^32 refused while 65 is accepted; an omitted bound accepted; nesting 5 accepted and 6 refused; typed source-handle declarations; compiler metadata and the topological invariant; exit condition true before the first iteration; declared-bound exhaustion (two runs, three evaluations, one limit outcome, fallback reached, exit route skipped); determinism across two runs; suspension inside a region resuming its own iteration without replay; nested loops charging per invocation; an unbounded loop reporting itself and exiting on its condition; and an unbounded loop still yielding to Stop. TypeScript: declared-loop acceptance, unbounded acceptance as a non-blocking warning, invalid bound and missing exit condition refused, and the editor's diagnostics for declared and unbounded loops.

Verification. Rust lib 437 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (one known order-dependent compaction test passes alone and on rerun). TypeScript 481 of 483 with tsc clean; the failures in the full parallel run are the long-standing 5-second timeouts in SettingsScreen.test.tsx, which passes 50/50 in isolation.

Give DSH-style iteration (the fitting part of tool-ralph and today's acyclic-only restriction) an Aworkit-native form, using the visible bounded loop the design already specifies.

Current state. The executable workflow contract rejects every cycle, so retry, refinement and feedback constructs cannot be authored even though the design's context/revision flow already models a visible bounded loop: evaluate a frozen exit condition at the loop header, admit another pass only within iteration/nesting/deadline/budget limits, and emit an explicit limit outcome on exhaustion. DSH's ralph is the counterpart, but its worker-self-reported completion does not fit Aworkit's frozen attempt/evaluator policy.

Design fit.
- Add a frozen loop construct to the node catalog and validate_v1_executable_catalog: a loop header node plus one declared feedback edge enclosing an explicit subgraph. The graph stays finite and compiler-verifiable, while the enclosed region repeats under a frozen exit condition.
- Replace the blanket cycle rejection with region-aware validation: only edges declared inside the loop region may close it; undeclared back edges remain hard errors; every node stays reachable from the input; nested loops are permitted only where the limits controller admits them.
- Each iteration appends a new immutable context revision on the loop lineage (no shared mutable state); the loop records its frame and charges ancestor budgets. Exhaustion produces an explicit LimitExceeded outcome routed by the frozen failure/fallback edge, never a silent stop.
- Execution is deterministic and inspectable: run details show loop frame, iteration index, exit-condition evaluation and the limit ledger. The editor renders the loop header with an explicit exit-condition panel and keeps acyclicity diagnostics for undeclared cycles.
- Completion is decided only by the frozen exit condition/evaluator, never by a worker's self-report, and an iteration never replays a settled side effect.

Non-goals. Unattended autonomous loops; unbounded iteration; loops that cross a Wait boundary or a Chat terminal state; DSH ralph's self-reported completion.

Outputs. Loop construct contract; compiler/validator and editor updates; context-revision and limit integration with provenance; run-details evidence; and tests for exit conditions, iteration/nesting/budget/deadline exhaustion, undeclared-cycle rejection, determinism, and no-replay recovery inside a loop.

data.title: Add bounded loop and feedback-edge constructs to the executable catalog
